instruction: Turn on Safe Browsing protection in Chrome's security settings to guard against dangerous websites.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":false,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Chrome menu -> Settings -> Privacy and Security -> Security. Found Safe Browsing section with Standard protection appearing selected. Model concluded it was already enabled and stopped without making changes. Evaluator returned 0 because safebrowsing was disabled in Preferences.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to Settings, click Privacy and Security sidebar, navigate to Security subsection, read and understand settings options
metadata.failure_analysis: Model misread UI state - saw Standard protection radio button as selected but safe browsing was actually disabled via Preferences config. Did not click to toggle/enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Same goal as original task (enable Safe Browsing) but with rephrased instruction that emphasizes 'turn on' as an active action and mentions 'security settings' to guide navigation. The model already navigated to the correct page, so a clearer instruction may help it actually click the toggle.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling Safe Browsing in Chrome security settings. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks enable_safe_browsing preference using exact_match, expecting 'true'. Same evaluator as original but with rephrased instruction.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_enable_safe_browsing correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and checks both safebrowsing.enabled and safebrowsing.enhanced fields, returning 'true' if either is set
Metric exact_match correctly compares getter result 'true' against expected 'true' via rules['expected']
Config properly disables safe browsing before task, establishing correct initial state
Postconfig restarts Chrome to ensure Preferences file is flushed to disk before getter reads it
Single-requirement instruction (enable Safe Browsing) is fully covered by the evaluator
